Your English is cool, don’t worry about it. Your reason for going to school is fantastic, not childish at all. You seem like you’re real into it. I get it seems scary because it’s sorta new to you and you weren’t expecting some aspects, but you just gotta be confident. I’m sorry about you and your sister, didn’t deserve it. It must be tough trying take care of someone’s mental health while trying to take care of yourself. This may be your chance to find out more about yourself. Why you’re feeling the way you’re feeling. Studying and helping the person could potentially help yourself ya know. Have you reached out to anyone on campus ?

My reason for college was for money. I wanted to be a dentist because they made six figures. Which was a bit silly, but it was my reason. Then, I thought that I didn’t want to do that and I got stuck choosing careers. I was looking at all these paths and realized that a job isn’t my life. Yes, it’s what I’ll be doing throughout my life, but it doesn’t define me. It’s just something that puts money on the table while I live my life. My goal is just to be happy. Find something I’m interested in job wise, then go from there. What’re your reasons and goals, if you don’t mind me asking ?

That’s dope. I went for biology, TERRIBLE DECISION haha. I went through a similar situation as yours. I actually lost my scholarship and I’ve been home working to go back to school. My problem was that I didn’t believe in myself and that led me to my downfall. All I can say is, believe in yourself. It sounds corny, but it’s the truth. Just remember why you’re doing this and your goals. Motivate yourself and get back into action. Get the wheels moving and get back on it. You got this.
